title: India's AI rules: from guidelines to a draft law
dek: India chose light-touch AI guidelines in 2025. A year later the government is preparing draft rules, funding homegrown models and asking where Indians' data goes.
seoTitle: India AI regulation 2026: MeitY rules timeline
bigLabel: Five-year budget of the IndiaAI Mission; MeitY told Parliament only a fraction has been released

glance.what: India published voluntary AI governance guidelines in November 2025 and hosted a global AI summit in February 2026. In October, IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw promised a consultation paper on AI rules covering safety and deepfakes, and the government is backing 20 homegrown AI models.
glance.why: The rules will decide how deepfakes are handled, what AI apps must tell you, how your data can be used to train AI, and how easily Indian startups can compete.
glance.next: The consultation paper was promised within a month of 8 October and is expected in November. Draft rules are open to public comment once published.

forYou: Once the consultation paper is out, anyone can send comments. Rules on deepfakes and AI labels could change what platforms must remove and what they must tell you.
next: MeitY's consultation paper, expected in November.

events.title: India AI Governance Guidelines
events.summary: The IT ministry unveils voluntary AI governance guidelines built on a 'do no harm' principle, favouring sandboxes for innovation over a new law.

events.title: AI Impact Summit and the New Delhi Declaration
events.summary: India hosts the AI Impact Summit at Bharat Mandapam. A non-binding New Delhi Declaration on inclusive, trusted AI is endorsed by countries including the US and China. OpenAI announces an 'OpenAI for India' partnership with Tata.
events.differs: Reports give 88 or 89 signatories, depending on when they were counted.

events.title: Minister promises draft AI rules within a month
events.summary: Ashwini Vaishnaw says the IT ministry will publish a consultation paper on AI within a month, covering AI safety, deepfakes and compliance for startups.

events.title: 'In the coming weeks'
events.summary: At the NDTV World Summit, Vaishnaw repeats that the consultation paper is coming in the next few weeks and will seek views from citizens, civil society and industry.

events.title: More homegrown models released
events.summary: Soket's Eka-1 and ZenteiQ's Dhir models join three earlier releases under the IndiaAI Mission. In all, 20 models are approved, being built by 12 startups including Sarvam and BharatGen.

events.title: Push for Indian AI in critical sectors
events.summary: The government is likely to push departments in sectors such as defence and aerospace to use Indian-built AI models and agents, MediaNama reports. It notes that MeitY has released only a fraction of the IndiaAI Mission's ₹10,371.92 crore budget.

events.title: Questions over home footage used to train robots
events.summary: IT Secretary S. Krishnan meets home-services apps and robotics firms over first-person video recorded by gig workers in Indian homes, and whether it is sold to overseas developers. Some executives ask the ministry to regulate such sales.
